sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Stephens County?
sections.html:
Two offices carry most of the work, and they sit in different buildings. The Tax Commissioner issues and collects the bills from Room 103 at 70 North Alexander Street in Toccoa, in the same government building as the county tag office. Weekday hours end at 4:45 in the afternoon. Call (706) 886-4753 or write to PO Box 187, Toccoa, GA 30577. The county site notes that the Tax Commissioner's website is maintained separately from the county's.

For values and homestead forms, call the Tax Assessor at (706) 886-7435. Returns also go there, because the county's funding page says the assessors, not the Tax Commissioner, were delegated that job in Stephens County. Appraisers who visit a parcel identify themselves with photo ID and a marked county vehicle, says the assessor page, usually after an appeal, a return or new construction.

sections.h2: Who pays which millage rates in Stephens County?
sections.html:
Three rates apply to every parcel: Georgia's, Stephens County's and the Stephens County School System's. A fourth, the Toccoa city rate, is added for homes inside Toccoa city limits, so an in-town house carries one more layer than a rural parcel that only uses a Toccoa mailing address.

Stephens County taxes 40 percent of a property's market value, and each mill of tax equals $1 per $1,000 of that taxed amount. The Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education pick the rates. A seller unsure whether the address is in city or county should ask the Tax Assessor which digest holds the parcel.

sections.h2: What are the Stephens County deadlines for returns, homestead and appeals?
sections.html:
Stephens County property tax dates and rules, from the county's Tax Assessor and Tax Commissioner pages
ItemRule
Who is chargedWhoever owns the property on January 1
Return seasonJanuary 1 through April 1, at the Tax Assessor
Same-year homesteadApply by April 1; a later filing waits for the next year
Bills on real estate and business personal propertyGenerally due November 15
Appeal of a noticeMust reach the assessors inside 45 days of the notice date
Skipping a required return10% on the value left off, plus interest
Refund of erroneous taxWritten claim to the commissioners within 3 years

The Tax Commissioner's website says refunds cover errors of fault, not valuation disputes. Business personal property needs a yearly return by April 1, and real estate owners with no changes can skip one.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions can Stephens County owners claim?
sections.html:
The county lists these exemptions on its homestead page, with the state code section for each:

  • Standard: $2,000 taken from the assessed value of the owner's primary residence, covering state, county and school tax, though municipal school levies are excepted.
  • Seniors 65 and up: an added local exemption, and another one if the owner's and spouse's net income did not top $10,000 the year before.
  • Age 62 school exemption: same $10,000 income ceiling, and it cannot exceed $10,000 of assessed value.
  • Floating inflation-proof exemption: owners 62 and up, with total household income under $30,000.
  • Disabled veterans: $50,000, passing to an unremarried surviving spouse or minor children.

Ownership and residence both have to be in place on January 1. The county says an exemption renews itself unless ownership changes, which means a buyer files fresh. A tax deferral is a further option for owners 62 and older at $15,000 of gross income or below. A state Homeowners Tax Relief Grant that once showed up as a bill credit was withdrawn in 2008.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Stephens County?
sections.html:
Census numbers for Stephens County: 27,854 people in mid-2025, up 4.0% from 26,780 at the 2020 base, spread over 12,461 housing units. Owners live in 73.6% of those units. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $175,300 and a typical rent is $820. Median household income is $54,754, and 23.3% of residents have passed 65.

The county covers 178.86 square miles of land at about 150 people per square mile, so most parcels are not in a compact city grid. The Census Bureau counts 36 building permits for 2025 against the 12,461 units already standing. Toccoa holds the Historic Courthouse at 37 West Tugalo Street, where the board of elections also works.

sections.h2: What else does the Stephens County Tax Commissioner collect that a seller should know about?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner's website says property is taxable in the county where it sits, and it lists categories beyond the house itself. Business equipment is assessed at 40 percent. Timber on the lot is treated differently, since it is taxed only when sold or harvested, and then at full market value. A seller with timber on the lot or business equipment in an outbuilding should ask the Tax Assessor how each is carried on the digest.

Vehicle owners renew their registration and pay ad valorem tax every year in the 30 day period that ends on their birthday, and a newly bought vehicle must be registered within 30 days. The tag office is in the Stephens County Government Building at 70 N. Alexander Street, Room 103, with weekday hours of 8:00 to 5:00. This registration is separate from the real estate bill.

Other deed related services listed on the county site include recording a plat, trade name registration and power of attorney filings, which can matter if an heir or an agent signs for the owner.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Stephens County?
sections.html:
The county's deeds page prints these numbers:

  • Transfer tax of $1 per $1,000 of money paid.
  • A $25 filing fee.
  • A $5 blank deed form.
  • 50 cents a page for copies.

Per recorded deed, fifty cents of that tax is kept by the county and the rest goes to the state. The grantor's signature must be witnessed and notarized, and the clerk can help calculate what is due.

Warranty deeds must carry a transfer tax form whether or not money changes hands, and the forms can be completed online at the state clerks' authority site. Filing a deed is not required for it to be legal, but the county says filing protects the owner. A closing attorney usually prepares the deed.

sections.h2: How do I pay or find a Stephens County tax bill?
sections.html:
Start at the county's Online Payments page, then use the Tax Assessor's online record search or tax estimator to look up a parcel.

A seller closing late in the year should agree with the buyer on who covers a bill charged to the January 1 owner. Call the Tax Commissioner for your parcel's balance ahead of any contract signing, and expect the payoff to come out of your sale proceeds. The Tax Commissioner's website warns that unpaid tax can lead to a levy and sale.

faqs.q: What is the usual payment date for a Stephens County tax bill?
faqs.a: The Tax Commissioner's website says real estate and business personal property bills are generally due November 15. Check the date on your own bill, or call (706) 886-4753.

faqs.q: When must a Stephens County homestead application be filed?
faqs.a: April 1. A later filing takes effect the year after. Applications go to the Tax Assessor, and you must have lived in the home on January 1.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window for a Stephens County assessment notice?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date, counted by when the appeal is received. The Tax Commissioner's website adds that an appeal the assessors do not settle moves to the Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Do Toccoa residents pay extra property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Residents inside Toccoa city limits pay the Toccoa city millage in addition to the Georgia, Stephens County and Stephens County School System millage.

faqs.q: What does the county charge in transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The county's deeds page prints $1 per $1,000 of money paid, with fifty cents per deed staying in the county. Ask the Clerk of Court to confirm the figure for your sale.
